paragraphs: In a little wooden house on the edge of a great forest lived a family of three bears: big, strong Papa Bear, kind-hearted Mama Bear, and Little Bear, who was always grumbling and complaining. The bears' home was very cosy, and they had exactly three of everything: three chairs around a large round table, three bowls and three spoons, three armchairs with three little books beside them, and three beds tucked beneath fluffy quilts.

Every morning, the bear family ate porridge made by Mama Bear. It was the best porridge in the world, with honey and blueberries. Mama Bear had learnt the recipe from Grandma Bear, and Grandma Bear had learnt it from Great-Grandma Bear. It had been in their family for generations.

One morning, the bears woke up especially early. The day was so beautiful that they decided to go for a walk in the forest. No sooner said than done! They got straight up from the table without even finishing their porridge, leaving their bowls behind.
The bears were not the only ones who thought it was a particularly beautiful day. A little girl with golden hair thought so too, and she set off for a walk at just the same time.
She was a rather naughty child, well known for getting into mischief. Unfortunately for the bears, her feet carried her straight to their little house at the edge of the forest.
When Goldilocks saw such a cosy cottage, her curiosity got the better of her manners. She went inside without being invited!

The moment Goldilocks stepped into the bears' house, she smelt the porridge. As you already know, it was the best porridge in the world, and Goldilocks was a very curious child. Without thinking about what might happen, she sat down at the kitchen table and pulled the first bowl towards her.
“This is too hot,” she said, putting a spoonful of Papa Bear's porridge into her mouth.
“This is too cold,” she said with a frown, after tasting a spoonful from Mama Bear's bowl.
“This is just right!” she cried, tasting a spoonful from Little Bear's bowl. Poor, poor Little Bear! Goldilocks gobbled up every bit of his porridge and even licked the bowl clean!

When she had finished, she hopped down from her chair and began looking around the cottage. In the sitting room, she found three lovely armchairs covered in yellow plush: a big one, a middle-sized one, and a little one. They looked very, very comfortable.
The little girl wanted to try them out at once.
“This is too stiff,” she said, climbing into Papa Bear's big armchair and trying a few little bounces.
“This is too bouncy,” she said with a frown, jumping into Mama Bear's middle-sized armchair and bouncing straight back up like a ball.
“This is just right!” she cried, settling comfortably into the smallest armchair, which belonged to Little Bear. Then suddenly, CRACK! One of its legs snapped, and Goldilocks landed on the floor.

After exploring the whole house, Goldilocks began to feel tired. So she went upstairs to the bears' bedroom, where she had already spotted three beds tucked beneath fluffy quilts. One was enormous, the next was a little smaller, and the third was very tiny indeed.
“This is too hard,” she said, lying down in the biggest bed.
“This is too soft,” she said with a frown, rummaging through the blankets on the slightly smaller bed.
“This is just right!” she said, climbing beneath the quilt on the third and smallest bed. And there she fell asleep.

Before long, the bears returned from their morning walk. Oh, what a strange sight met their eyes! The cottage door was standing wide open, although they clearly remembered shutting it when they left. Something was wrong!
The bears went over to the table where they had left their porridge and rubbed their eyes in amazement.
“Someone has been eating my porridge,” boomed Papa Bear in his deep, rumbling voice, peering into his bowl.
“And mine too,” said Mama Bear in surprise.
“Waaah!” wailed Little Bear the Grumbler. “Someone has eaten every bit of mine!”
Wary and watchful, the bears went into the sitting room to see whether the intruder had caused any trouble there too. They began examining their armchairs in great surprise.
“Someone has been sitting in my armchair,” boomed Papa Bear in his deep, rumbling voice.
“And mine too,” said Mama Bear, looking worried.
“Waaah!” wailed Little Bear the Grumbler. “Someone has broken a leg off my armchair!”
Finding nothing else downstairs, the bears climbed the stairs to their bedroom. To their great surprise, they found their beds all rumpled and untidy.
“Someone has been sleeping in my bed,” grumbled Papa Bear angrily.
“And mine too,” said Mama Bear.
“Waaah!” wailed Little Bear the Grumbler. “Someone is still sleeping in my bed!”

The bears' voices woke Goldilocks. She blinked three times, then caught sight of the three bears standing over her and screamed in fright! She sprang to her feet and leapt straight out of the window into the bushes below the cottage. Without looking back, she ran as fast as she could.
But as Goldilocks ran through the forest, her conscience began to trouble her.

“What have I done?” she thought. “I ate someone else's porridge. I broke someone else's armchair. And I made a mess in someone else's bedroom.” She stopped running. “I can't leave things like this. I must put everything right!”
Slowly, with her head hanging low, she went back to the bears' cottage and knocked timidly on the door. Papa Bear opened it and asked with a stern expression:

“What sort of behaviour is this, young lady? Don't you know that you mustn't go into someone else's home without being invited? Or eat their porridge? Or break their furniture? Or make a mess in their bedroom?”
“I'm sorry, sir. I behaved very badly. I'd like to put everything right, if you'll let me!”
Just then, kind-hearted Mama Bear peeped out from behind Papa Bear.
“After an apology like that, I think we ought to give her a chance,” Mama Bear said to Papa Bear. With a friendly gesture, she invited Goldilocks inside. “Come in, little girl. Welcome to our home.”

Goldilocks spent the whole day with the bears. First, she helped Mama Bear make a fresh batch of porridge. Then she helped Papa Bear mend the broken armchair. Finally, she and Little Bear made all the beds.
When the work was done, she sat down to supper with the bears and shared the best porridge in the world. There was even cake for pudding: not too sweet, not too bland, but just right.

Everyone knows that making mischief isn't good behaviour, but there isn't a child who doesn't get into trouble now and then. What matters most is always saying sorry and putting right whatever you have done wrong.
That sort of behaviour is “just right” too.
